name: Athreos
description: Athreos is the God of Passage on Theros, a veiled ferryman who guides the dead across the river to the Underworld.

summary.text: Athreos is the God of Passage on Theros, a veiled ferryman who guides the dead across the river to the Underworld.

bio.text: He gathers the newly dead and ferries them across the river, taking funerary masks or a gold coin as payment.

citations.text: Theros: card flavor text (Theros, 2013), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.
"Tragedy". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Oct 2013. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: Erebos sent him to take the oracle Daxos to the Underworld, and despite Karametra's efforts he seized the boy until Lidia offered herself in his place.

citations.text: "Athreos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Erebos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Daxos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: The mortal Phenax escaped the Underworld wrapped in Athreos's cloak, unnoticed by him, and Athreos despises him for cheating death.

citations.text: "Phenax", section "Underworld". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Phenax", section "Divine Relationships". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Odunos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: During the Silence of the Gods Athreos became inactive, so souls could not be ferried and Returned accumulated outside the Underworld.

citations.text: "Athreos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: During the Phyrexian invasion he shattered Kroxa's chains so it could destroy the Phyrexians, and sent his hound Kunoros to accompany and restrain it.

citations.text: "Athreos", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Athreos", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kroxa", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

status.text: Athreos is still the god guiding the dead, and the last event shows him sending Kunoros to restrain Kroxa in the Underworld.

citations.text: "Athreos", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

citations.work: Theros Beyond Death Promos: card flavor text
citations.text: Theros Beyond Death Promos: card flavor text (Theros Beyond Death Promos, 2020), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Lidia takes Daxos to Athreos; he speaks and is revealed to be an oracle; Erebos sends Athreos to claim him.
timeline.quote: Athreos was sent to claim the child

citation.text: "Daxos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Lidia trades herself for her son and Karametra's emissary takes Daxos to safety.
timeline.quote: Lidia traded herself for her son

citation.text: "Daxos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Erebos sends Athreos to fetch Daxos for his oracular gift; Lidia takes her son's place and is brought to the Underworld.
timeline.quote: thus she was brought to the Underworld while Daxos was left alone in the Mortal Realm.

citation.text: "Erebos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Originally a mortal trapped in the Underworld, Phenax hides from Erebos and Athreos by forsaking his identity and crosses back wrapped in Athreos's cloak, becoming the first Returned.
timeline.quote: This escape established his role as the first Returned and set him on the path to godhood.

citation.text: "Phenax", section "Underworld". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Phenax becomes the first mortal to escape the land of the dead by using the Tartyx's waters to strip himself of identity.
timeline.quote: Phenax was the first mortal to find a route of escape out of the land of the dead

citation.text: "Returned", section "Origins". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Penthikos reaches the river's edge and meets a robed woman who tells him he has no face to pay the boatman.
timeline.quote: You bring no face for the boatman. How will you cross?

citation.text: "Tragedy". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Oct 2013. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Penthikos defies fate and crosses the river, paying his crystallized mask to the ferryman.
timeline.quote: The price paid, we drifted across to that bleak land.

citation.text: "Tragedy". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Oct 2013. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Erebos sends Athreos to take Daxos to the Underworld; despite Karametra's efforts Athreos seizes the boy, and Lidia offers herself in his place and is taken instead.
timeline.quote: Lidia offered herself in her son's place and was taken to the Underworld instead.

citation.text: "Athreos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: During the Silence of the Gods, Athreos becomes inactive, souls cannot be ferried, and Returned accumulate outside the Underworld.
timeline.quote: Athreos, like the other deities of Theros, became inactive.

citation.text: "Athreos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Leandros prays to Athreos for the dead as the squad moves on without burying them.
timeline.quote: Leandros muttered a prayer to Athreos, who ferried souls to the Underworld

citation.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Ravos strikes a deal with Athreos to guide the dead in exchange for yearly visits with his lover.
timeline.quote: Ravos swore to help Athreos guide the dead to the Underworld in exchange for seeing his dead lover once each year.

citation.work: It's Time to Talk Commander (2016 Edition)!
citation.text: "It's Time to Talk Commander (2016 Edition)!" by Magic Creative Team. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Oct 2016.

timeline.summary: The squad finds Eumalos and his squad dead and headless, then is trapped by a boulderfall.
timeline.quote: They were all dead, their heads missing.

citation.text: "Leandros", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Phenax becomes the first mortal to escape the Underworld unnoticed by Athreos or Erebos.
timeline.quote: Phenax was the first mortal to escape the Underworld without drawing the notice of Athreos or Erebos

citation.text: "Odunos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: At the River of the Dead a scholar of Athreos refuses him passage until a death mask forms on his face.
timeline.quote: he felt the matter on his face shift and sculpt itself into a grimacing death mask

citation.text: "Penthikos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Penthikos is ferried across to the Underworld to take his place among the dead.
timeline.quote: the ancient barge silently slid forth from the fog

citation.text: "Penthikos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: During the Phyrexian invasion, Athreos shatters Kroxa's chains so it can destroy the Phyrexians in the Underworld.
timeline.quote: Athreos shattered the chains that bound the titan, allowing it to lay waste to the Phyrexian forces.

citation.text: "Athreos", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Athreos sends Kunoros to accompany and restrain Kroxa so it cannot escape the Underworld.
timeline.quote: Athreos sent his hound, Kunoros , to accompany and restrain the titan during its rampage.

citation.text: "Athreos", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Athreos broke Kroxa's chains, and entrusted Kunoros to guide him against the Phyrexians.
timeline.quote: Athreos chose to break Kroxa’s chains

citation.text: "Kroxa", section "Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
